chunks.arabic_text: رِجَالُ الْكَشِّيِّ: حَكَى بَعْضُ الثِّقَاتِ بِنَيْسَابُورَ أَنَّهُ خَرَجَ لِإِسْحَاقَ بْنِ إِسْمَاعِيلَ مِنْ أَبِي مُحَمَّدٍ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ تَوْقِيعٌ

translations.en: Rijal al-Kashshi: One of the trustworthy narrators in Naysabur reported that a Tawqi [signed rescript] came out addressed to Ishaq b. Ismail from Abi Muhammad (peace be upon him)

chunks.arabic_text: يَا إِسْحَاقَ بْنِ إِسْمَاعِيلَ سَتَرَنَا اللَّهُ وَآيَاكَ بِسَتْرِهِ … فَإِذَا وَرَدْتَ بَغْدَادَ فَاقْرَأْهُ عَلَى الدِّهْقَانِ وَكِيلُنَا وَثِقَتُنَا وَالَّذِي يَقْبِضُ مِنْ مَوَالِينَا …

translations.en: O Ishaq b. Ismail, may Allah protect both you and us with His protection … so when you reach Baghdad then read it [this Tawqi] to al-Dihqan, our Wakil [agent], our Thiqa [trustworthy one], and the one who collects from our followers [the dues].

en.summary: This rescript (Tawqi) from Imam al-Mahdi (peace be upon him) to Ishaq ibn Ismail highlights the institutionalized financial system of the Shia community during the Minor and Major Ghaibah, specifically designating al-Dihqan as the trusted agent (wakil) for collecting khums and other dues. The mention of 'our followers' (mawalina) underscores the communal bond and the Imam's direct oversight of their economic contributions, a key element in Shia jurisprudence regarding the distribution of religious funds.
en.seo_question: Who is al-Dihqan and what was his role in the Shia community according to the Imam's rescript?

key_terms.تَوْقِيع: Tawqi (signed rescript or letter from the Imam)
key_terms.الدِّهْقَان: Al-Dihqan (a specific historical figure, agent of the Imam)
